item.title: Form 1004-E: Proposal for Reclassification: Form 1004-E: Proposal for Reclassification
item.content:encoded:
http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/deathbygin-2

A short tale for my authored article SCP-5118.

Spoiler / Explanation
Minimize

As Dr. Atmos gather information from Dr. Williams, it's implied that SCP-5118 is actually a dog who is a reality bender, turned human, and turned back into a dog when about to be captured. Evidence to support this includes:

  • SCP-5118 did not act like most other reality benders do when discovering they have powers (usually by hiding them from others).
  • SCP-5118 manifests chocolate, grapes, and soda - all things a dog cannot eat.
  • SCP-5118 appeared to be smiling while being chased.
  • SCP-5118 does not attempt to breach containment because it's current living situation is already ideal (it gets a bed, new toys, guaranteed food and water, and socializes with staff daily when they provide it with food).
  • Using it's powers while in containment would risk exposing itself. Since it's implied that it's "original form" is already a dog, the scans / tests from the SCP article would show nothing.

I wanted to write this tale to add a twist to the article without making this the clear-cut canon. Please let me know what you think.

item.title: My (First) SCP: Forum Criticism Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Sharkingdom Studios,

As per the Draft Forum Policies, new authors are to get their concepts reviewed and greenlighted by two experienced reviewers on the Idea Critique Forums before posting on the Draft Critique Forums.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can give assistance in developing an idea before a draft is written. They can also assist in letting you know if something similar exists on the site already, or inform you of various clichés/pitfalls to be cautious of. These elements are more effectively addressed earlier in the writing process.

If you would like to request a draft review without greenlights, you can use the IRC Chatrooms to solicit critique.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note the thread in which you received them, or the users whom provided them.

item.title: Looking for feedback: Re: Looking for feedback
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

My overall feeling regarding this is: so what?

There's weird little implications scattered throughout: from the handprints fitting Tradias' hand to the holes appearing to the change of the things movement corresponding to a flight; but none of these feel like they piece together into a coherent whole? Like, it's dangerous and it's heading towards someone but…why?

There's little structural things like the actuality of what a Centimane event is being the last thing described; when really saying what it is and then when it will happen would be more effective; and a general feeling of your ConProcs/Description paragraphs being unassociated sentences over a coherent paragraph; but fundamentally, my issue is that at the end, this doesn't give me enough pieces to collapse it into a whole that feels satisfying.

It kinda feels like this has a lot of opportunity for some really evocative description of the hands and stuff, particularly within the video log, but instead it feels like it spends a lot of time having Tradia mumble about being lost or what the air is like, and it feels like it just…needs more content there? Like you could theoretically cut basically everything Tradia says out the log and it'd still convey much the same thing; and indeed it's only really the final four action notes that actually convey things, and I'm left…wanting? Even if it's just more of an emotional arc from Tradia where we can see him go from calm and collected and scientific at the start to running scared and frightened at the end (which, he does but it's conveyed entirely through his behaviour with only a few hints in the dialogue).

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

Guards are to be patrollingpatrol the area around SCP-X in routines 1 hour apart.

'in routines 1 hour apart' feels unclear: if you mean e.g. 'with 1 hour between patrols', perhaps that would be a clearer phrasing?

In the case of a Centimane event, nearby human population centers will be evacuated under the pretense of an unavoidable future dust storm.

I'd probably add a paragraph break here cos of the change in topic from guard patrols to Centimane events; and I'd lean towards moving the part of the description describing them to a footnote here

After the evacuation of the population center, SCP-X will be closely monitored for the point where it exits the area. Afterward, Foundation funds will go into repairing the damage done to buildings and other structures by SCP-X.

This kinda implies these two things are related but they aren't quite; it feels like the 'point where it exits the area' needs a little more clarification around why it's important for this to work.

SCP-X is a geoglyph located in an uninhabited desert area in ██████.

This feels like a weird redaction; it kinda feels like this would be more effective if we knew where it was so we can imagine what places are in danger.

The lines making up SCP-X are, on average, 1.5cm deep, 3cm thick, and stylized in the shape of a human hand, covering roughly 24km2.

This phrasing is ambiguous as to whether each individual line looks like a human hand or the overall geoglyph looks like a human hand.

If you want the second, I'd add replace the comma between '1.5cm deep' and '3cm thick' with an and, and change the comma after 'thick' to a semi-colon. If you want the first, I'd separate the region they're covering into a separate sentence.

being capable of traveling 17m in a day.

I feel like this could do with a more evocative word than 'travelling'

Most electronic devices that are put inside of SCP-X malfunction, leading to difficulty in finding possible internal anomalous phenomena within SCP-X.

'Most' is needlessly vague here imo. I'd either cut it, or give an indication of what causes some electronic devices to break. Same goes for 'malfunction' tbh.

Most electronic devices that are put inside of SCP-X malfunction, leading to difficulty in finding possible internal anomalous phenomena within SCP-X. Any attempts at installing barriers to prevent the movement of SCP-X have been met with failure. The soonest possible date of a Centimane event is 3 years and 163 days. See Addendum X-01.

These three sentences don't feel like they belong in the same paragraph: they're all completely disconnected ideas with no flow from one to the next to the last.

On 07/10/20██, Agent Johnathan Tradia was tasked with an exploration mission into SCP-X to ascertain any other possible anomalous properties.

I'm not a fan of this redaction; I'm not sure why when this occurred would be sensitive information.

Tradia. ]

this space is unnecessary; here and every where you use it.

[Tradia proceeds walking for two minutes and thirty-seven seconds. ]

Walking where?

Agent Tradia: Huh, the ground in here seems pretty weird. It's stretchy, it's kinda like a trampoline.

Why does it take Tradia like, 2.5minutes to notice this?

Tradia resumes walking for approximately three minutes before turning around, showing multiple hand-shaped indentations on the ground. The handprints form a line leading to Tradia. ]

Missing an opening [ here

On 08/12/██ SCP-4440 ceased movement, rotated 37° clockwise, and resumed movement resulting in a delay of 73 days until a Centimane event will occur.

1) this is a bad redaction again

2) This addendum as a whole doesn't really feel like it builds off what came before.

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Elevator: Re: Elevator
item.content:encoded:
Heyo! I'll come and crit your draft you. Keep in mind I'm not clincal tone pro, so this'll largely be a 'what I think in general' type crit.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

SCP-XXXX is located at what was previously known as █████ Inc.

Generally, redacting/blackboxing something in the ConProcs (Special Containment Procedures) isn't a good idea. Realistically speaking, redacting information in the ConProcs doesn't make sense in-universe. These are the procedures—made as simple and basic as possible for personnel—for containing something. Redacting part of the information would just make the job more difficult than it needs to be.

Also, even out of ConProcs, I don't really see a reason to redact the name of a location. In universe, you're being granted clearance to read a classified article. Knowing where it came from usually isn't going to be that bad.

and administered Class A Amnestic.

Put 'a' between 'administered' and 'class'.

Following the unauthorized use of SCP-XXXX, no personnel under level four clearance are allowed in the same building as SCP-XXXX.

Probably a personal thing, but 'below level four clearance' sounds better than 'under'.

elevator shaft.The

Put a space between 'shaft.' and 'The'.

The elevator itself is comprised of steel and has seven buttons on the inside of it.

Remove 'itself'. Intuition says it's a tad unclinical to put it there.

SCP-XXXX functions as a normal elevator but when button seven is pressed the person(s) inside the elevator will be taken to the place they most desire to go.

'most desire to go' sounds off.
Let's try, 'SCP-XXXX functions as a normal elevator, but when the seventh button is pressed, the person(s) inside will be transported to a location they subconsciously desire.'

Inside is a GPS that records the places it has gone.

Let's try, 'Inside is a GPS that keeps records of previously traversed locations.'

The elevator will not work without it.

'The elevator will not function without the GPS.'
That said, I'm not sure how to feel about this line. I assume the GPS is just planted in the elevator. Also, this implies that the personnel have tried…removing it? I don't see why they'd do that.

Places recorded have been The Fiji Islands, low Earth orbit, and England.

I think you can merge this with an earlier sentence to turn it into:
'Inside is a GPS that keeps records of previously explored locations, examples including The Fiji Islands, low Earth orbit, and England.'

It's cleaner and smoother.

In all instances the elevator returns within 20 minutes after leaving the facility area.

Puts a comma after 'instances'

Always talked of "the fields".

Hmmm you can change 'of' to 'about' and it would be better, but it still sounds unclinical.

Maybe, 'Frequently mentioned a location he referred to as, 'the fields.'

personnel.Camera feed was choppy but the surroundings were normal.

Space after 'personnel.'

You should bold out 'Dr. Spencer's Diary' whenever you write down the entries. It makes it stand out and look cleaner.

'Foundation' should be capitalized because it's a proper noun.

The elevators GPS showed the word unkown on the location.

'GPS displayed 'unknown' as the location.'

Results: D-7586 appeared to have died of asphyxiation, presumably from being subjected to outer space.

I don't really like the way this is worded. 'Appeared to have died of asphyxiation, presumably from being subjected to outer space.'

You could just say that D-7586 died from exposure to outer space. It's been stated plainly thus far that the elevator takes you to where you want to go.

'Presume: suppose that something is the case on the basis of probability.'

There really isn't much probability here.

Apologies if this part sounds kinda overly nitpicky.

D-4576 was a surfer. She lived on the beach and says that is where her heart is. D-4576 is very kind to all personnel considering the situation she is in.

Clinical tone is meant to portray something as emotionlessly as possible. This passage reads a little too much like normal prose.
We could change it to, 'D-4576 once had a significant interest in surfing. She lived on a beach prior to becoming D-Class. She has been cooperative thus far.'

Even then, I'm not sure mentioning the cooperative part is necessary. Unless she shown shown be to uncooperative beforehand.

When D-4576 arrived back at the facility she was covered in sand. She stated it was the best day she has had in forever. Her dopamine levels were extremely high.

Second sentence is too emotional. Adjectives like 'extremely' are usually non-clinical.

Test 4 reads…super awkwardly. As well as the diary entry beforehand.

Also, the reference to SCP-682 wasn't a good move because references/cross-links nowadays are frowned upon.

This was a strange piece to critique, considering this is a greenlit idea with a draft from over a year ago. I looked at the edit history and see that it was updated a few days ago, yes, but it still feels…strange. I'll detail this more in my final thoughts collapsible.

+Final Thoughts
-Final Thoughts

All in all, I'm not sure how to feel about this. 'Get in thing and go to desired/weird locale at push of button/drop of hat' isn't anything new, but it's always the execution that matters more than the concept. Everything has already been done in storytelling history, it's about what you do with a thing to differentiate it that makes it special.

But from what I've seen of your current draft, it's really standard with sub-clinical tone, bizarre and not really believable diary entries and a plot that essentially equates to 'these test logs freak me out and I'm afraid I might die. GG, fuck this.'

I should let you know that I, myself, am still pretty new here and I wasn't here in 2019; I joined a few months ago as of me writing this down. From what I've heard and seen, generic testing logs with little information aren't really good anymore.

I've heard one person say that testing logs aren't really good anymore, period, but like I think you could make this SCP work if you…say…

Did more in depth logs with video logs and such. Strap a video cam to some D-Class, have them go through some stuff and extend each test log to being a mini-adventure. Pretty standard stuff, but there's always an audience for that.

Also, you'll need to incorporate the researcher more organically into the story rather than have them write some extremely barebones diary entries.

Maybe they could maintain communication with the test D-Class subjects during test logs?

From what I've seen of your current logs, they essentially stick D-class in the thing, wave goodbye and tell them to be back before dinner. That doesn't really make sense considering the D-Class can just leave and not come back.

All in all, I hope everything I wrote made sense and I hope I helped. Good luck with this piece. I hope you continue pursuing this because it's nice to contribute to a lovely site like this ^_^
